behaviors.description: Maintain reversible terrain-piece removal in the current session from a world-fixed tetrahedral tiling at 0.65 m lattice spacing. Neighboring pieces share displaced vertices and triangular interfaces; geological occupancy trims surface and cave pieces. Aim selects a stable piece identity independently of viewing direction. Removed pieces are empty for rendering, aiming and cave contact. Aim-oriented pyramid stamps are explicitly retired from normal gameplay; old box and pyramid edits remain supported. Refilling restores the original material. Retain blade-footprint cuts for physical tool experiments. Shared cut data drives presentation, radial height queries and the native tool collider. Legacy parabolic excavation and opt-in saves remain retained experiments; default sessions start fresh.
behaviors.selection: Legacy excavation operations remain retained experiments; default gameplay sessions do not restore or persist their cuts. Existing old saves are archived once rather than destroyed.

checks.expectation: Surface simulation has declared OGC preparation, advancement and release routes.
Surface cuts affect navigation and visible geometry, survive a save/reload, and release simulation resources appropriately.
checks.procedure: Run tetrahedral tiling tests for shared interfaces, nondegenerate volumes, gap-free unique ownership and planet-scale identity. Run mining_checks for remove/refill collision and direction-independent piece selection. Review surface state and serialization; check excavation, repeated cuts, navigation over the result, save/reload, bounded simulation and close/failure cleanup. Reopen a version-1 save with fragments overlapping the new terrain; verify retained data and inactive material, no startup OGC configuration, and no save loading during cleanup after graphics preparation fails. With persist_excavation false, verify an existing surface save is archived and new sessions have no retained holes. No save rewrite is permitted in this mode.

checks.expectation: Numeric CollisionSnapshot, GameCollision and Update transport uses the registered caller/ownership routes and invocation trace. Water receives the same accepted geometry without round-tripping unchanged terrain through JSON.
checks.procedure: Run water snapshot revision/indexing regressions and release mining benchmark with water enabled. Exercise moving debris, unchanged snapshots, removed debris and stale revision rejection. The JSON hooks remain available.

behaviors.description: Preserve the shared surface baseline while selecting traversable support below the player inside the configured cave volume. Include cave data in scene, acoustic and water-collision snapshots.
behaviors.selection: Selected with CaveSystem and Procedures/caves.json. It does not implement underground rock fracture or replace accepted tool/material accounting.

checks.expectation: Walking through an entrance can descend below the former surface. Walls/ceilings remain collidable, reset returns to the surface, and sound/water use the same cave void.
checks.procedure: Source-only first pass; inspect and run passage traversal, support, reset, water and sound checks separately when execution is authorized.

behaviors.description: RefineMaterial transfers ownership of an occupied material volume from its implicit rest representation to explicit matter. This is resolution refinement, not removed-volume accounting. Frame, player/cave support, water collision and appearance share ownership domains. Closing clears session ownership together with its physical owner.
behaviors.selection: PhysicsSystem.GameStep/GameClose. Supersedes MaterialPatch and the atlas-ground-plus-specimen approach at the user request of 2026-10-29. No fixed twelve-site quota; storage remains bounded at 4096 regions. Session material is not serialized.

checks.expectation: Replacement accepts physical material before hiding static ground; closing/resetting restores the static world and removes session masks.
checks.procedure: Compile and inspect named hook declarations; user observes excavation, walk-away/return, reset, pause and close. Compilation does not verify play behavior.

behaviors.description: November 12 geography supersedes the former forest-at-spawn and repeated Ridge and Valley terrain. Distances are metres relative to town at X=125, Z=-125; +X is east. Open plains precede a forest from +1000 to +21000, retaining the existing forest species and density; a desert reaches the cliff-and-beach coast near +28000. A roughly 1550 m north-south mountain ridge at -8000 separates the town from plains and a city at -11000. The desert city is at +24500. Shared height, soil and ocean connectivity drive visible and physical ground. A bounded visual ocean mesh extends to 15.36 km beyond the local water patch; it is clipped against the shared analytic coast without replacing local collision or water occupancy.
behaviors.selection: Default Wormwood surface; Nightworld keeps its independent terrain.

checks.expectation: Forest membership begins exactly 1 km east and ends at 21 km; the western ridge exceeds 1100 m along its north-south extent; plains beyond it stay low, desert ground is sand, and eastern water has a continuous ocean bed and rough surf.
checks.procedure: Run terrain::regions tests and regional water/material integration tests. Review rendered regional views and traverse the coast in the native game; numeric tests alone do not establish visual quality.

behaviors.description: North is -Z and distances are metres from town. A northwest-sloping forest edge begins 1 km north and joins the eastern forest. The northern sea spans 6 to 11 km north and 30 km east-west, from 9 km west to 21 km east. Across it a forest extends to 41 km north, where permanent treeless snow begins. Shared ground height, material, vegetation and water classification follow the same geography.
behaviors.selection: Default surface outside Nightworld; separate southern geography remains retained.

checks.expectation: The northwest wedge connects to the east forest; the sea has a submerged bed and correct shore directions on all four sides. Land continues for 30 km beyond the sea, then snow replaces turf and trees. Banks remain continuous.
checks.procedure: Run northern_ terrain tests and regional_ocean tests; review native northern forest, sea, polar ground and ice-city views separately. Unit checks do not establish native appearance or travel performance.

behaviors.description: An all-longitude coastline 16 km south of town leads to a 40 km sea, a rounded 100 by 100 km snowy island with ocean on both sides, another 100 km sea, and a rounded jungle continent with 4000 by 4000 km chart extents starting 256 km south. Arc-length coordinates prevent a mirrored southern continent. Jungle has wet green soil, evergreen broadleaf forest with a distinct procedural profile, sandy shores and a city clearing 1 km inland. This is an authored southern island, not the geometric pole. Distant jungle crowns reuse the existing broadleaf atlas at tropical tree scale; near trees use the evergreen procedural profile. Original southern surface colors use authoritative biome material sampling without reconstructing the town cave color tiles.
behaviors.selection: Default overworld southern geography; preserve independent Nightworld and northern geography.

checks.expectation: Sea samples are submerged; snowy and jungle interiors are dry; the polar island ends east and west, jungle ends after 4000 km; no antipodal duplicate. Tree identities round-trip. Snow has the existing physical Snow substance and its surface color; jungle retains evergreen foliage through winter.
checks.procedure: Run southern_ tests, export_southern_globe ignored diagnostic, and native southern scene review. Inspect coast continuity and native collision separately from cartographic output.
